knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

McKenna et al. built an in vitro pharmacokinetic / pharmacodynamic (PK/PD)
model of doxorubicin in four triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cell lines.
A three-compartment cellular PK model (Eqs 1-3) describes uptake of the drug
from the well medium and its binding to DNA. Its output, the maximum bound
intracellular concentration CB,max, summarises a timed exposure and drives a
treatment-response model of cell number over the following ~30 days
(Eqs 4, 5A, 5B and 10).

The cell lines were fitted independently, so the library carries one PK
model and one PD model per cell line (eight models):

```{r models}
lines_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  line = c("SUM-149PT", "MDA-MB-231", "MDA-MB-453", "MDA-MB-468"),
  sfx = c("sum149pt", "mdamb231", "mdamb453", "mdamb468")
) |>
  mutate(
    pk = paste0("McKenna_2017_doxorubicin_", sfx, "_pk"),
    pd = paste0("McKenna_2017_doxorubicin_", sfx, "_pd")
  )
pk_ui <- lapply(setNames(lines_tbl$pk, lines_tbl$line), function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
pd_ui <- lapply(setNames(lines_tbl$pd, lines_tbl$line), function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
lines_tbl |>
  select(line, pk, pd) |>
  rename("Cell line" = line, "PK model" = pk, "PD model" = pd) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

* Citation: `r pk_ui[[1]]$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-05902-z>
  (open access; supplementary materials at the same address)

## How the two models are used together

1. Simulate the PK model with the treatment's medium concentration time course.
   A treatment is a bolus of the applied concentration (nM) into `conc_dox`
   at t = 0; media replacement at the end of exposure is an `evid = 5`
   replacement of `conc_dox` by 0.
2. Take CB,max, the maximum of `intracellular_bound`. Bound drug is never
   released (Eq 3), so CB,max is the bound concentration once the free pool
   has washed out. Simulate long enough for that (a day or two after removal;
   the slowest line, MDA-MB-453, washes out with a half-life of about 4 h).
3. Simulate the PD model with `CBMAX_DOX_NM` set to that value, dosing the
   initial cell number into both `cells_a` and `cells_b` at t = 0. The output
   `cells` is the cell number per well.

```{r helpers}
# CB,max for one treatment: medium concentration conc_nm (nM) for texp hours.
cbmax_of <- function(ui, conc_nm, texp, horizon = 720) {
  ev <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = c(0, texp), evid = c(1, 5), amt = c(conc_nm, 0), cmt = "conc_dox"),
    data.frame(time = c(texp, horizon), evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "intracellular_bound")
  )
  ev$id <- 1L
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  max(out$intracellular_bound)
}

# Cell-number trajectory for one treatment. The paper initialised each fit at
# the first post-treatment count, so the cells are dosed at t_start with n_start.
cells_of <- function(ui, cbmax, times, n_start, t_start = 0) {
  ev <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = t_start, evid = 1, amt = n_start, cmt = c("cells_a", "cells_b")),
    data.frame(time = times, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cells_a")
  )
  ev$id <- 1L
  ev$CBMAX_DOX_NM <- cbmax
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out <- out[!duplicated(out$time), ]
  out[match(times, out$time), c("time", "cells", "cells_a", "cells_b")]
}
```

# Population

The models describe cultured human TNBC cell lines, one from each of four
Lehmann subtypes: MDA-MB-468 (basal-like 1), SUM-149PT (basal-like 2),
MDA-MB-231 (mesenchymal) and MDA-MB-453 (luminal androgen receptor).

* **Uptake (PK) experiment.** About 10,000 parental cells per well of a 96-well
  plate, 250 uL of medium, imaged every ~15 min by brightfield and
  fluorescence microscopy from 1 h before to ~24 h after drug application.
  Doxorubicin's own fluorescence, converted to concentration with a linear
  calibration (Fig 2d), gave intracellular and extracellular concentration
  time courses. Doxorubicin was applied at 312-2500 nM (two-fold series) for 6
  or 12 h, in duplicate.
* **Treatment-response (PD) experiment.** About 2,500 H2B-mRFP-labelled cells
  per well, grown for at least 3 days, then exposed to 9.77-2500 nM (nine
  two-fold concentrations) for 6, 12 or 24 h and imaged daily for at least 30
  days, six replicate wells per condition. Media were refreshed every 3 days.

The same information is in each model's `population` metadata, for example
`pd_ui[["SUM-149PT"]]$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries a comment naming its source. The tables below
collect them. Figure values were digitised by the maintainers from the
published figures (main-text figures from the 300 dpi images in the article
PDF; supplementary figures from the supplement PDF).

## Equations

| Equation | Model | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| `d/dt(conc_dox) = kFE vI/vE CF - kEF CE` | PK | Eq 1 |
| `d/dt(intracellular_free) = kEF vE/vI CE - (kFE + kFB) CF` | PK | Eq 2 |
| `d/dt(intracellular_bound) = kFB CF` | PK | Eq 3 |
| `d/dt(cells_x) = (kp - kd(t)) N (1 - N / theta)` | PD | Eq 4 |
| `kd(t) = kd,A` for t >= 0 | PD (`cells_a`) | Eq 5A |
| `kd(t) = kd,B r t exp(1 - r t)` for t >= 0 | PD (`cells_b`) | Eq 5B |
| `cells = w_A cells_a + w_B cells_b` | PD | Eq 10 (weights from the AIC, Eqs 8-9) |
| kd,A, kd,B, r, theta_A, theta_B, w_B as functions of CB,max | PD | Fig 5, Fig S7, Fig S8 (knots digitised, see below) |

## PK parameters

```{r pk-trace}
pk_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pk_ui), function(l) {
  th <- pk_ui[[l]]$theta
  tibble::tibble(
    line = l,
    kEF = exp(th[["lkef"]]),
    kFE = exp(th[["lkfe"]]),
    kFB = exp(th[["lkfb"]]),
    vE = exp(th[["lvext"]]),
    vI = exp(th[["lvint"]])
  )
}))
pk_tab |>
  mutate(vI = signif(vI, 4)) |>
  rename(
    "Cell line" = line,
    "kEF (1/h)" = kEF,
    "kFE (1/h)" = kFE,
    "kFB (1/h)" = kFB,
    "vE (uL)" = vE,
    "vI (uL)" = vI
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "kEF, kFE, kFB: bar heights of Fig 2f-h. vE: Methods (250 uL per well). vI: back-solved, see below.")
```

## PD parameters

The proliferation rate kp and the untreated carrying capacity theta are
printed in the Results ("Doxorubicin treatment response"). The drug-effect
parameters were fitted separately for every concentration x exposure
condition. Plotted against CB,max, the fits from the three exposure series
fall on one curve per cell line (Fig 5). The model encodes each curve as 11
knots on the two-fold dilution lattice: knot 0 is the 9.77 nM x 6 h condition
and knot n the condition with 2^n times its medium AUC, located at
`cbmax_n00 * 2^n`. The knot value is the mean of the digitised points of the
6, 12 and 24 h series at that knot (one or two series at the ends of the
lattice).

```{r pd-trace}
pd_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pd_ui), function(l) {
  th <- pd_ui[[l]]$theta
  tibble::tibble(
    line = l,
    kp = exp(th[["lkgrow"]]),
    theta = exp(th[["lcellmax"]]),
    cbmax_n00 = th[["cbmax_n00"]]
  )
}))
pd_tab |>
  rename(
    "Cell line" = line,
    "kp (1/h)" = kp,
    "Control theta (cells)" = theta,
    "CB,max at knot 0 (nM)" = cbmax_n00
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "kp and control theta: Results text. cbmax_n00: from the companion PK model.")

knots <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pd_ui), function(l) {
  th <- pd_ui[[l]]$theta
  nm <- grep("_n[0-9]{2}$", names(th), value = TRUE)
  nm <- setdiff(nm, "cbmax_n00")
  tibble::tibble(line = l, name = nm, value = unname(th[nm])) |>
    mutate(
      par = sub("_n[0-9]{2}$", "", name),
      knot = as.integer(sub("^.*_n", "", name)),
      cbmax = th[["cbmax_n00"]] * 2^knot
    )
}))
knots |>
  filter(line == "SUM-149PT") |>
  select(par, knot, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = par, values_from = value) |>
  rename(
    "Knot" = knot,
    "kd,A (1/h)" = kda,
    "kd,B (1/h)" = kdb,
    "r (1/h)" = ron,
    "theta_A (cells)" = thetaa,
    "theta_B (cells)" = thetab,
    "w_B" = wb
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "SUM-149PT knot values (Fig 5, Fig S7, Fig S8). The other cell lines are in their model files.")
```

## The intracellular volume vI

The paper estimated vI as the 10,000 seeded cells times a cell volume from an
ellipsoid fit to the segmentation, but does not print it. kEF (about 1e-5 1/h)
only acts through the product kEF vE / vI, so vI is needed. For a single
exposure pulse the PK model is linear and the free pool washes out completely,
so

CB,max = kFB / (kFE + kFB) x kEF x vE / vI x AUC,

where AUC is the medium concentration times the exposure time. Figs 3 and 4
print CB,max next to the AUC for 20 conditions. The maintainers set vI per
cell line so that CB,max / AUC equals the geometric mean of those printed
ratios. The implied cell volumes are 507, 2645, 187 and 479 um^3 (equivalent
spheres 10, 17, 7 and 10 um across). The MDA-MB-453 value inherits the
imprecision of its very short kEF bar, but CB depends only on the product
kEF vE / vI, which the printed CB,max values fix.

# Validation of the PK model

## CB,max against the values printed in Figs 3 and 4

PKNCA computes Cmax of the bound concentration (that is, CB,max) and the medium
AUC for each printed condition. The reference values are the numbers printed
in the panel legends of Figs 3 and 4.

```{r pk-printed}
printed <- tibble::tribble(
  ~line, ~conc, ~texp, ~cbmax_pub, ~auc_pub, ~fig,
  "SUM-149PT", 2500 / 128, 6, 3.2, 117, "3a",
  "SUM-149PT", 156.25, 6, 25.5, 938, "3d, 4",
  "SUM-149PT", 312.5, 6, 50.9, 1875, "4",
  "SUM-149PT", 625, 6, 101.8, 3750, "4",
  "SUM-149PT", 1250, 6, 203.6, 7500, "3g",
  "SUM-149PT", 2500 / 128, 12, 6.0, 234, "3b",
  "SUM-149PT", 156.25, 12, 47.8, 1875, "3e",
  "SUM-149PT", 1250, 12, 382.1, 15000, "3h",
  "SUM-149PT", 2500 / 128, 24, 11.9, 469, "3c",
  "SUM-149PT", 156.25, 24, 95.4, 3750, "3f",
  "SUM-149PT", 1250, 24, 763.2, 30000, "3i",
  "MDA-MB-231", 156.25, 6, 17.2, 938, "4",
  "MDA-MB-231", 312.5, 6, 34.4, 1875, "4",
  "MDA-MB-231", 625, 6, 68.7, 3750, "4",
  "MDA-MB-453", 156.25, 6, 18.1, 938, "4",
  "MDA-MB-453", 312.5, 6, 36.3, 1875, "4",
  "MDA-MB-453", 625, 6, 72.6, 3750, "4",
  "MDA-MB-468", 156.25, 6, 12.8, 938, "4",
  "MDA-MB-468", 312.5, 6, 25.7, 1875, "4",
  "MDA-MB-468", 625, 6, 51.3, 3750, "4"
) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = sprintf("%s %s nM x %g h", line, formatC(conc, format = "g", digits = 4), texp),
    id = row_number()
  )

pk_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(printed)), function(i) {
  p <- printed[i, ]
  tt <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 72, by = 0.25), p$texp - 1e-4, p$texp + 1e-4, 168, 720)))
  ev <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = c(0, p$texp), evid = c(1, 5), amt = c(p$conc, 0), cmt = "conc_dox"),
    data.frame(time = tt, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "intracellular_bound")
  )
  ev$id <- 1L
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(pk_ui[[p$line]], ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out <- out[!duplicated(out$time), ]
  tibble::tibble(
    id = p$id, treatment = p$treatment, time = out$time,
    conc_dox = out$conc_dox, intracellular_bound = out$intracellular_bound
  )
}))

dose_df <- printed |> transmute(id, treatment, time = 0, amt = conc)
iv <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 720, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

# CB,max = Cmax of the bound concentration
nca_cb <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk_sim, intracellular_bound ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = transform(iv, auclast = FALSE)
))
# Medium AUC = AUClast of conc_dox
nca_auc <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk_sim, conc_dox ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = transform(iv, cmax = FALSE)
))

sim_both <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_cb) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax"),
  as.data.frame(nca_auc) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")
) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_both,
  reference = printed |> transmute(treatment, cmax = cbmax_pub, auclast = auc_pub),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "nM", auclast = "nM*h"),
  tolerance_pct = 5
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Cmax is CB,max (bound concentration) and AUClast is the medium AUC.",
    "Reference: Figs 3 and 4 panel legends. * differs from the reference by more than 5%."
  )
)
```

```{r pk-printed-check}
chk_pk <- printed |>
  left_join(
    sim_both |> pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  mutate(cb_pct = 100 * (cmax / cbmax_pub - 1), auc_pct = 100 * (auclast / auc_pub - 1))
stopifnot(
  # The medium AUC labels are concentration x exposure time, rounded.
  all(abs(chk_pk$auc_pct) < 1),
  # One vI per cell line, set from the same printed values: MDA lines
  # reproduce to rounding, SUM-149PT to its exposure split (next section).
  all(abs(chk_pk$cb_pct[chk_pk$line != "SUM-149PT"]) < 1),
  all(abs(chk_pk$cb_pct) < 5)
)
```

The three MDA lines reproduce the printed CB,max values to within rounding.
For SUM-149PT, the printed CB,max per unit AUC is 6.6% higher for the 6 h
exposures (0.0271-0.0273 nM per nM*h) than for the 12 and 24 h exposures
(0.0254-0.0256). No single set of linear PK parameters produces that
difference: with the free pool washing out within hours (kFE + kFB =
1.48 1/h), CB,max is proportional to AUC whatever the exposure time. The model
uses one value between the two groups, so the 6 h conditions come out about
3.5% low and the 12 and 24 h conditions about 3% high. The paper does not say
how the input function was specified for each series. One possibility is that
the 6 h input used the observed removal time; the media replacement in Fig 2e
happens about 6.7 h after application, not at 6 h.

## Uptake time course

The uptake experiment (Fig 2e shows one well at 2500 nM for 6 h) can be
simulated directly. The intracellular concentration `cint` is the sum of the
free and bound pools, which share the intracellular space.

```{r fig2e, fig.cap = "Simulated total intracellular doxorubicin after 2500 nM for 6 h, compare Fig 2e (cell line of Fig 2e not stated)."}
up <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pk_ui), function(l) {
  ev <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = c(0, 6), evid = c(1, 5), amt = c(2500, 0), cmt = "conc_dox"),
    data.frame(time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "intracellular_bound")
  )
  ev$id <- 1L
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(pk_ui[[l]], ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out <- out[!duplicated(out$time), ]
  tibble::tibble(line = l, time = out$time, cint = out$cint, bound = out$intracellular_bound)
}))
up |>
  pivot_longer(c(cint, bound), names_to = "pool") |>
  mutate(pool = recode(pool, cint = "total intracellular", bound = "bound")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = line, linetype = pool)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Doxorubicin (nM)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

In Fig 2e the measured intracellular concentration rises to about 400 nM by
the end of a 6 h exposure to 2500 nM and then declines slowly. The simulated
values at 6 h are of the same order (about 490-770 nM). The slowly declining
shape matches the slow-exchange lines MDA-MB-453 and MDA-MB-468.

# Validation of the PD model

## Drug-effect parameters against CB,max (Figs 5, S7 and S8)

```{r fig5, fig.height = 9, fig.cap = "Model drug-effect functions (lines) through the digitised knots (points). Replicates Fig 5 (kd,A, kd,B, r), Fig S7 (theta_A, theta_B) and Fig S8 (w_B) of McKenna 2017, pooled over the 6, 12 and 24 h series."}
grid <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pd_ui), function(l) {
  cb0 <- pd_ui[[l]]$theta[["cbmax_n00"]]
  cbs <- cb0 * 2^seq(0, 10, by = 0.05)
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(cbs), time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cells_a", CBMAX_DOX_NM = cbs)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(pd_ui[[l]], ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  tibble::tibble(
    line = l, cbmax = cbs, kda = out$kd_a, kdb = out$kd_b, ron = out$ron,
    thetaa = out$theta_a, thetab = out$theta_b, wb = out$w_b
  )
}))
lab <- c(
  kda = "kd,A (1/h)", kdb = "kd,B (1/h)", ron = "r (1/h)",
  thetaa = "theta_A (cells)", thetab = "theta_B (cells)", wb = "w_B"
)
grid_long <- grid |> pivot_longer(-c(line, cbmax), names_to = "par")
ggplot(grid_long, aes(cbmax, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = knots, colour = "red", size = 1) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_grid(par ~ line, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(par = lab)) +
  labs(x = "CB,max (nM)", y = NULL)
```

The paper states two values that the interpolation must carry:

* SUM-149PT: above an AUC of 25,000 nM*h the population declines rapidly with
  kd,A >= 2.9e-2 1/h (Results, "Doxorubicin treatment response"). The only
  such condition in the design is 1250 nM for 24 h (and 2500 nM for 12 h,
  the same AUC of 30,000 nM*h).
* SUM-149PT: w_B is about 1 at low CB,max and about 0 at high CB,max
  (Fig S8 caption and Results).

```{r printed-pd-check}
cb_hi <- cbmax_of(pk_ui[["SUM-149PT"]], 1250, 24)
kda_hi <- approx(grid$cbmax[grid$line == "SUM-149PT"], grid$kda[grid$line == "SUM-149PT"], cb_hi)$y
wb_sum <- grid$wb[grid$line == "SUM-149PT"]
c(cbmax_1250nM_24h = cb_hi, kd_a = kda_hi)
stopifnot(
  # 2.9e-2 printed to two figures; the digitised knot sits at 2.92e-2-3.00e-2
  kda_hi >= 0.0285,
  wb_sum[1] > 0.95,
  tail(wb_sum, 1) < 0.05
)
```

## Cell-number trajectories (Figs 3 and 4)

The red bands in Figs 3 and 4 are the 95% confidence intervals of the
paper's best fit to each condition. The maintainers digitised the centre of
each band every 50 h, starting at the first post-treatment time point
(25 h). Each simulation starts from the band centre at 25 h, as the paper
initialised its fits at the first post-treatment count, and keeps t = 0 at
drug application.

The published bands come from fits to each individual condition. The library
model instead takes all its drug-effect parameters from the pooled
curves above, so it behaves like the paper's prediction scheme, not like
its per-condition fits.

```{r bands}

  group_by(fig, line, conc, texp) |>
  mutate(time = 25 + 50 * (row_number() - 1)) |>
  ungroup()

traj <- bands |>
  group_by(fig, line, conc, texp) |>
  group_modify(function(z, key) {
    cb <- cbmax_of(pk_ui[[key$line]], key$conc, key$texp)
    tt <- seq(25, max(z$time), by = 5)
    s <- cells_of(pd_ui[[key$line]], cb, tt, n_start = z$mid[z$time == 25], t_start = 25)
    tibble::tibble(cbmax = cb, time = s$time, cells = s$cells)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(panel = sprintf("Fig %s: %s %g nM x %g h", fig, line, signif(conc, 3), texp))
bands <- bands |> mutate(panel = sprintf("Fig %s: %s %g nM x %g h", fig, line, signif(conc, 3), texp))
# Short facet labels: Fig 3 is all SUM-149PT, Fig 4 is all 6 h exposures
short_lab <- function(fig, line, conc, texp) {
  ifelse(fig == "3", sprintf("%g nM x %g h", signif(conc, 3), texp), sprintf("%s, %g nM", line, signif(conc, 3)))
}
traj <- traj |> mutate(facet = short_lab(fig, line, conc, texp))
bands <- bands |> mutate(facet = short_lab(fig, line, conc, texp))
```

```{r fig3, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "SUM-149PT after 20, 156 and 1250 nM for 6, 12 or 24 h. Lines: library model; points: centre of the published best-fit band. Replicates Fig 3 of McKenna 2017."}
ggplot(filter(traj, fig == "3"), aes(time, cells)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = filter(bands, fig == "3"), aes(y = mid), colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~facet, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after drug application (h)", y = "Cells per well")
```

```{r fig4, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Four cell lines after 156, 312 and 625 nM for 6 h. Lines: library model; points: centre of the published best-fit band. Replicates Fig 4 of McKenna 2017."}
ggplot(filter(traj, fig == "4"), aes(time, cells)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = filter(bands, fig == "4"), aes(y = mid), colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~facet, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Time after drug application (h)", y = "Cells per well")
```

```{r traj-check}
chk_pd <- bands |>
  left_join(traj |> select(panel, time, cells), by = c("panel", "time"), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (cells - mid) / mid)
per_panel <- chk_pd |>
  group_by(panel) |>
  summarise(
    "median % difference" = round(median(pct), 1),
    "median |% difference|" = round(median(abs(pct)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(per_panel, caption = "Library model against the centre of the published best-fit band, per panel.")
stopifnot(
  # A wrong knot table, CB,max scale or growth constant moves whole panels
  # by tens of percent; the pooled interpolation itself is not exact.
  median(abs(chk_pd$pct)) < 15,
  quantile(per_panel[["median |% difference|"]], 0.9) < 40
)
```

The model follows most panels closely. The largest differences are in
panels where regrowth starts late. There the published per-condition fit
and the pooled curves place the onset of regrowth at different times (for
example SUM-149PT at 1250 nM for 12 h, whose published band is wide; see
Fig 3h). This matches the paper's own finding that its predictions were less
accurate at the highest concentrations (Table 1).

## Untreated growth (Fig S3)

With `CBMAX_DOX_NM = 0` the model is the control logistic growth with the
printed kp and theta.

```{r control, fig.cap = "Untreated growth from 2,500 cells per well. Compare Fig S3."}
ctrl <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pd_ui), function(l) {
  s <- cells_of(pd_ui[[l]], 0, seq(0, 720, by = 6), n_start = 2500)
  tibble::tibble(line = l, time = s$time, cells = s$cells)
}))
ggplot(ctrl, aes(time, cells, colour = line)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cells per well", colour = NULL)
end_ctrl <- ctrl |> filter(time == 720) |> left_join(pd_tab, by = "line")
stopifnot(all(abs(end_ctrl$cells / end_ctrl$theta - 1) < 0.01))
```

## Example: a regimen outside the experimental design

The framework was built to predict untested regimens. As an example, here
are all four cell lines after 400 nM for 18 h (medium AUC 7200 nM*h):

```{r example, fig.cap = "Predicted response to 400 nM for 18 h from 2,500 cells per well."}
ex <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pd_ui), function(l) {
  cb <- cbmax_of(pk_ui[[l]], 400, 18)
  s <- cells_of(pd_ui[[l]], cb, seq(0, 720, by = 6), n_start = 2500)
  tibble::tibble(line = sprintf("%s (CB,max %.0f nM)", l, cb), time = s$time, cells = s$cells)
}))
ggplot(ex, aes(time, cells, colour = line)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after drug application (h)", y = "Cells per well", colour = NULL)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Figure-derived values.** The paper prints no table of model parameters
  apart from kp and the control theta. The maintainers digitised kEF, kFE
  and kFB from the bar charts of Fig 2f-h, and the per-condition drug-effect
  parameters from Fig 5 (kd,A, kd,B, r), Fig S7 (theta_A, theta_B) and Fig S8
  (w_B). Fig 5 and Fig S7 were read by locating each marker on the two-fold
  dilution lattice. Fig S8, where most weights are exactly 0 or 1 and lines
  jump between them, was read by eye to about +/-0.02. The MDA-MB-453 kEF
  bar is only 4-5 pixels tall in the 300 dpi figure, so its value is
  uncertain by about 15%. This affects only the derived vI, not CB.
* **The drug-effect functions are the maintainers' construction.** The paper
  maps a new treatment's (CB,max, AUC) to parameters by local linear
  regression, and to model weights by a binomial logistic model trained on the
  fitted weights. It prints neither the regression bandwidth nor the logistic
  coefficients. The library replaces both with piecewise-linear interpolation
  in log2(CB,max) through the knot means. For the pulsed exposures studied,
  CB,max is proportional to AUC (to within the 6.6% SUM-149PT exposure split
  discussed above), so CB,max alone indexes the treatment and AUC adds no
  separate information. For other input shapes (for example in vivo
  biexponential curves) the two would differ, and the paper's regression used
  both.
* **Averaging across exposure series.** Each knot is the mean of the 6, 12 and
  24 h fits at that CB,max. Where the series disagree (for example the
  SUM-149PT w_B at knot 5, where the 24 h fit selected Eq 5A and the 6 and
  12 h fits selected Eq 5B), the mean is a weight between 0 and 1.
* **Outside the lattice.** CB,max values below knot 0 or above knot 10 are
  clamped to the end knots. `CBMAX_DOX_NM = 0` is the untreated control (no
  drug effect, control carrying capacity), which is a discontinuity: the
  lowest tested exposure has a small negative kd (growth slightly faster than
  control) in SUM-149PT and MDA-MB-231.
* **vI back-solved.** See "The intracellular volume vI" above. The CB,max
  of the PD model's knot 0 (`cbmax_n00`) is the PK model's value for the
  9.77 nM x 6 h condition, so the two models share one CB,max scale.
* **Pre-treatment phase not modelled.** The paper fitted kp to at least 3
  days of pre-treatment growth. The library models start at drug application
  (t = 0), with the cell number at that time (or at the first post-treatment
  count, as in the comparison above) supplied as a dose into both
  `cells_a` and `cells_b`.
* **No variability.** The paper fitted deterministic models by nonlinear least
  squares and reports confidence intervals from bootstrapping, but no
  between-well variance or residual-error model. None is encoded.
* **Media replacement** at the end of exposure is an `evid = 5` replacement of
  the medium concentration by zero, as in the experiment. The 3-day media
  refreshes during the PD experiment contain no drug and do not change CB,max.
* **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on the
  publisher's article page or in Europe PMC as of 2026-11-25.
